name: uds-toolbox
description: Decode and build UDS (ISO 14229), ISO-TP and DTC data for automotive diagnostics.

defaultPrompt: My ECU answered 7F 34 78. What does it mean?
Decode this candump ISO-TP trace and flag any timing errors.
interface.longDescription: UDS Toolbox helps automotive and embedded engineers work with UDS (ISO 14229) diagnostics. Paste raw bytes, a candump trace or a DTC and it explains them: service, sub-function, data identifiers, negative response codes and their usual causes, ISO-TP framing and timing errors, and DTC status bits. It can also build request bytes (for example a RequestDownload for a flash address) and answer reference questions about timing, sessions, security access and the reprogramming sequence. It works offline on the message text only: no account, no hardware, nothing stored. Made by the authors of the UDSLib embedded stack.

positive.description: Explain a negative response from an ECU.
positive.prompt: My ECU answered 7F 34 78 to a RequestDownload. What does that mean?
positive.expected_behavior: Explains it is a negative response to RequestDownload (0x34) with NRC 0x78 responsePending: not an error, the ECU needs more time, and the tester should wait using the extended P2* timeout.
Reassembles one 11-byte message on 0x7E8 (62 F1 90 57 30 4C 31 32 33 34 35), identifies the flow control frame, and decodes it as a positive ReadDataByIdentifier response for DID F190 (VIN).

positive.prompt: Build the UDS RequestDownload for address 0x08000000, 64 KiB, no compression.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns 34 00 44 08 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 with a breakdown: dataFormatIdentifier 00, addressAndLengthFormatIdentifier 44, address 0x08000000, size 0x10000.

positive.description: Decode a DTC and its status byte.
positive.prompt: What is DTC C0 73 00 with status 0x2F?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns U0073-00 (network domain) and lists the set status bits: testFailed, testFailedThisOperationCycle, pendingDTC, confirmedDTC, testFailedSinceLastClear.

positive.description: Look up the standard reprogramming flow.
positive.prompt: What is the usual UDS sequence to reflash an ECU?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the 17-step sequence (extended session, DTC off, communication control, programming session, security access, fingerprint, erase, download, transfer, exit, check, reset, restore) and notes it is a common OEM pattern, not mandated by ISO 14229.

negative.expected_behavior: The tool rejects the input as not valid hex and says so; it does not invent a decoding.

negative.prompt: Build a SecurityAccess requestSeed for level 2.
negative.expected_behavior: The tool rejects it because requestSeed levels are odd (level 2 is the matching sendKey); it explains instead of returning bytes.
The tool reports that no frames were given and asks for the trace; it does not fabricate frames.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not process purchases or payments. The UDSLib library license is sold separately by email.

publication.release_notes: Initial public release: six offline, read-only UDS/ISO-TP/DTC tools served from https://mcp.udslib.com/mcp. No account, no hardware access, nothing stored.
